# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–37 (Updated 2026-10-13, Final Revision 5)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Spring of tenth year after Waterloo (1831). Story spans from Sunday, 26th April dinner (Chapters 1–35) through Chapter 36 (winter into summer) to Chapter 37 (spring). Emperor of China dinner scheduled Monday, 8th July; election for Westminster borough Tuesday, 9th July (three weeks ahead as of Chapter 35). Chapter 37 primarily set in Harrowgate hill farms (Mirecombe, Yarlton, Dunholt), market towns (Bryngate, Salwick), Lowestoft, and London.
- **Key Locations**: London (Welbeck Street, Grosvenor Square, Abchurch Lane, Beargarden Club, Bruton Street, Queen's Gate, Islington, City Road Music-Hall, Cannon Street Hotel); Coventry Island; Queen's Crawley; Southend; Harrowgate; coastal towns (Lowestoft, Penzance, Brighton, Salwick); rural areas (Sheep's Acre Farm, Staveton, Bryngate, Beccles, Caversham, Pickering).

## Major Deaths
John Sedley, Mr. Osborne, Joseph Sedley, Colonel Rawdon Crawley, Sir Pitt, Wevie Lindner (died winter, buried Salmere).

## Rebecca's Arc
Never became Lady Crawley; styles herself so. Son (Sir Rawdon) receives allowance but refuses to see her. Appears wealthy at Bath/Cheltenham, busies herself with piety and Charity Lists.

## Amelia and William Dobbin
Married at Ostend; Amelia initiated encounter. Dobbin quit service, rented "the Evergreens" (Hampshire). Devoted father; daughter Jane his pride.

## Lady Carbury and Family

**Lady Carbury**: Welbeck Street resident with Felix and Henrietta. Authored "Criminal Queens." Crushed by "Evening Pulpit" review; praised by "Morning Breakfast Table" (Mr. Broune). Rejected Mr. Broune's proposal via letter by six o'clock evening, sent via Didon to Pall Mall East. Full of regrets; in debt. Chapter 36: Attended soirée with Roger Carbury; found Paul and Henrietta together upon return. Disbelieved accidental visit claim. Cross-examined Henrietta on intentions. Allowed Henrietta to leave after kissing. **Chapter 37: Expressed wonder at Alf (editor of "Evening Pulpit"), noting he has sailed "within the wind" but now risks three or four thousand pounds in legal expenses.**

**Felix Carbury**: Beautiful; cynosure of mother's eyes. Won £2,000 from Lord Grasslough, £400 from Miles Grendall at gaming. Director of South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway. Won £200 cheque from Melmotte if withdrew from Marie. **Chapter 37: Amenable to elopement with Marie Thursday week from Liverpool noon. Didon "very urgent" he recover funds to Melmotte. Frequently at City Road Music-Hall. When Ruby pressed marriage demand, refused outright: "Marry, Ruby! No, I don't ever mean to marry." Deemed marriage beneath his baronetcy. Plans New York departure as escape. Resolved on elopement despite written promise to Melmotte; anticipates quarrel "thoroughly internecine" upon discovery. Visited Melmotte in city; received £200 cheque (not full amount promised); seeking to recover more funds.**

**Henrietta Carbury**: Rejected Roger's suit (too young, age disparity). Paul returned "as still dear friend" within week, promising not to see her three months. Wore rose from Roger's room. Roger declared love anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Paul thoroughly in love with her. Chapter 36: Paul visited her at Welbeck Street in Lady Carbury's absence. Told mother she loves someone else and praises Roger as "rock of strength" who "never lies."

## Ruby Ruggles and Suitors

**Ruby Ruggles**: Granddaughter of Daniel Ruggles (Sheep's Acre). Pretty with long glossy ringlets. **Chapter 37: Working as servant/maid to Mrs. Pipkin (her aunt) at Islington who lets lodgings with five children. Very fond of dancing. Danced with Felix at City Road Music-Hall. When Felix refused marriage demand, Roger Carbury visited her at Mrs. Pipkin's house. Ruby disclosed her grandfather Daniel Ruggles had pulled her by hair when undressed, nearly getting into bed—witnessed by Sally Hockett. She fled for protection. Roger warned Felix "is as bad as bad can be...would ruin you and cast you from him without a pang." Praised John Crumb as noble, loving, wanting only her happiness and respectability. Ruby found conviction borne upon her though struggling against it. Roger warned if Felix and John Crumb were alone together, something would happen to Felix. Extracted promise she would not see Felix again. His words weakened her admiration for Felix. Roger spoke to Mrs. Pipkin about Ruby's late hours and promised further steps to keep watch over her.**

**John Crumb**: Country lover from Suffolk, "Bungay mealman." Chapter 35: After supper, moved to take Ruby's hand; Ruby fled. Rode to Carbury Hall searching for her. **Chapter 37: Visited Roger at Carbury Manor. Expressed anguish about Felix "pulling of her about"; declared willingness to "swing for it" if Felix seduced her. Expressed depths of woman's character confound him. Roger assured him Ruby was good girl and promised further supervision by Mrs. Pipkin. Crumb's purpose of journey to London after Saxmundham fair was shaken. Resolved to send Mrs. Pipkin price of new blue cloak via Mixet's letter and money order. Has no literary skill beyond bill-making.**

**Daniel Ruggles**: Holds Sheep's Acre Farm on bishop's lease; Roger Carbury's tenant. **Chapter 37: Violent under gin and water; pulled Ruby by hair when undressed (witnessed by Sally Hockett). Told Roger "whoever it is ought to speak out his mind"; says "a girl has to mind herself."**

## The Melmottes

**Augustus Melmotte**: Chairman, South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Company. Big man with large whiskers; expression of mental power on harsh vulgar face. Rumours of gigantic swindler. Candidate for Westminster parliament seat. Planning Emperor of China dinner (8th July) and Westminster election (9th July). **Chapter 37: Extremely busy with electioneering speeches, Committee members, dinner orders, commercial affairs. Told Felix: only entitled to shares for £600 now, will see it put right. To Paul, proposed Mexican embassy with instructions and expense cheque; tone dubious to Paul. Expressed relief dinner would be over, noting "It's a deal easier to make a treaty with an Emperor, than to give him a dinner." Received Board meeting call; obliged to run off to meeting of gentlemen connected with interior of Africa at Cannon Street Hotel.**

**Marie Melmotte**: Speaks English well; forming own opinions. Rejected Lord Grasslough. **Chapter 37: Elopement plan with Felix confirmed: Travel to Liverpool Thursday week, board S.S. "Adriatic" at noon bound for New York. Marry on board or at New York. Return within month to force father's acceptance. Didon to pose as aunt; Felix as "Smith"; Marie as French girl. Had key to Grosvenor Square gardens; Didon to unlock gate. Marie obtained £200; awaits Felix's recovery of more funds.** Engaged to Lord Nidderdale (Chapter 35).

## The Longestaffes

**Sir Merton Longestaffe**: Determined no London expenses; family will not return from Caversham. Desires to sell Pickering and disembarrass Caversham from debt. Dolly refused consent unless half produce given to him. **Chapter 37: Attended Board meeting; astonished at its brevity and minimal his involvement. Miles Grendall read from book (incomprehensible), chairman read figures, Cohenlupe declared unprecedented prosperity, meeting ended. Wished to speak with Melmotte but was informed he ran off to Cannon Street Hotel meeting.**

**Adolphus (Dolly) Longestaffe**: Has rooms in Bruton Street. **Chapter 37: Arrangement made: £5,000 pay off all tradesmen's debts, leave him comfortably possessed; other £20,000 make his property free. Went to Caversham, made his own terms; father unable to move him. Returned to father early morning (about two o'clock) demanding cheque on Melmotte's bank payable to his own. Has not yet received single ten-pound note from sale. Threatens to employ Mr. Squercum (lawyer) if money not paid quickly.**

**Georgiana Longestaffe**: Made protest against Melmottes. Following morning received invitation to stay with them. By Sunday, present at Grosvenor Square.

## South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Scheme

**The Enterprise**: Railway from Salt Lake City, branching from San Francisco/Chicago line, through New Mexico/Arizona into Mexico, terminating Vera Cruz. Approximately 2,000 miles. Stock at par; shares sold at premium. Directors understood fortune made by floating shares, not building railway.

**London Directorate**: Melmotte (chairman), Lord Alfred Grendall, Sir Felix Carbury, Samuel Cohenlupe (MP for Staines), Lord Nidderdale, Paul Montague.

## Paul Montague and Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle

**Paul's Situation**: Living at Beargarden. Junior railway firm member. Dislikes Fisker. Thoroughly in love with Hetta. **Chapter 37: Visited Mrs. Hurtle at Islington evening. She received warmly, explained recent absence to Southend with Mrs. Pipkin and baby. At Lowestoft: Paul encountered Roger Carbury by chance while with Mrs. Hurtle. Blushed upon seeing Roger, left Mrs. Hurtle's arm, shook hands. Roger introduced coldly with coldest ceremony. Mrs. Hurtle equally cold, surmising Roger no friend to her. Roger spoke severely: "I did not know that you were thinking of coming to Lowestoft." Roger later reproved Paul: allowing himself entrapped into promise of marriage, then breaking it for adequate reasons does not justify living with lady afterwards on terms inducing supposition old promise holds good. Stated should have said Paul threw her over. Meeting by chance as he did, how not to speak? Believes lady will succeed in marrying Paul. Paul thought of gentleman in Oregon and certain difficulties in leaving. Roger counselled: marriage with her would be destruction; should tell her mind and leave her. Advised Paul must go in and eat dinner. At hotel dining-room: Mrs. Hurtle was radiant with smiles but Paul sensed something forced; she waited until waiter departed. Asked if Roger was hardly civil to her. Paul acknowledged Roger disapproves of her. Mrs. Hurtle questioned whether Paul had made Roger understand his purpose, criticizing his silence. Paul plucked up courage to tell her he could not join his lot with her—chiefly because his heart is elsewhere, and because her antecedents had caused all his friends to warn him against such marriage. Mrs. Hurtle argued: when she had sworn he would be her God upon earth, was that bitter? A woman alone must fight her own battles; tongue is her weapon. Asked him to speak "that one word" to marry her. Reminded him of his own urgent prayers and oaths to her; she had spoken her word because she loved and believed him; asked him to give what he swore he had given before. When Paul explained he had written to her, she responded with fury: "Wrote to me! And I was to take that as sufficient!" Declared she would travel world's surface to face injustice. Clenched fist on knife, then dropped it further away. Insisted his letter could not break their bond; his conduct since her arrival in country has already contradicted it. Confessed before he could spare her: shot a man in Oregon and brought him down dead; she saved herself—without that act, must have destroyed herself afterwards. Asked why they did not try her for murder and why women flocked to kiss her garments' hems. Claimed his soft civilization knows nothing of such necessity. Stated she had not concealed her former husband Caradoc Hurtle's character—he was drunkard and scoundrel; she had fought him as one fights cruelty, falsehood, fraud, treachery. Standing armed, she guarded her bedroom door, told him he would enter only over her body; he went to tavern for a week. Acknowledged a certificate of his existence exists in back of Texas, five hundred miles from Galveston, but immaterial to Paul. She was divorced from Caradoc Hurtle according to Kansas law on grounds of cruelty and drunkenness; he made no appearance; Court granted it. Insisted she is not disgraced. When Paul pressed details of her prior statement about Caradoc's death, she said she believed him dead and did not remember precisely what was said before. Now has made her property again her own. Demanded: why is she condemned if not for protecting herself from drunken violence, saving her life from reprobate husband, and securing her property by law?**

**Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle**: Formerly betrothed to Paul. Arrived Wednesday. During earlier engagement promised to follow him; renewed promises in New York. Theatre evening: Paul took her. Does not like Frenchmen; prefers Englishmen to Americans. Thinks he should marry her or world hear story of his perjury. Most fond of baby. Unwell, weak and cowardly; eyes show only love.

## Roger Carbury
Nearly forty. Never owed shilling he couldn't pay. Firmly opposed Melmotte connection on principle. Works as priest on day-labourer's wages. Soft heart; knows Lady Carbury false and Felix worthless. Declared love to Henrietta anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. **Chapter 37: Visited Ruby at Islington; warned her forcefully against Felix; praised John Crumb's nobility and love; extracted promise she would not see Felix again. Spoke to Mrs. Pipkin about Ruby's late hours. Encountered Paul and Mrs. Hurtle by chance at Lowestoft. Greeted them coldly; reproved Paul severely regarding his conduct with Mrs. Hurtle. Counselled Paul that marriage with her would be destruction and advised him to tell her mind and leave her.**

## Minor Characters
**Lord Alfred Grendall**: Elder Grendall. **Chapter 37: Nearly overwhelmed by electioneering; declared willingness to help Melmotte but nearly in rebellion: "If this goes on much longer I shall cut it." Burdened with seating arrangements for dinner; doesn't know rank precedence; relies on Herald's office fellow.**

**Miles Grendall**: Secretary to Melmotte. Does not pay debts of honour. **Chapter 37: Read from book at Board meeting (incomprehensible). Explained to Longestaffe that Melmotte ran off to Cannon Street Hotel meeting.**

**Didon**: Marie's attendant; facilitates elopement plan; to receive £50 before boarding ship. "Very urgent" with Felix to recover funds to Melmotte.

**Father John Barham**: Priest, Beccles.

**Mrs. Pipkin**: Ruby's aunt at Islington; lets lodgings with five children. Most fond of baby. Roger spoke to her about Ruby's late hours.

**Sally Hockett**: Witnessed Daniel Ruggles pulling Ruby by hair.

**Mr. Squercum**: Lawyer threatened employment by Dolly if money not paid quickly.

**Chapter 37 Provincial Figures**: Orvie Hollett (swore to plant orchard above Yarlton); Eldette (disputes oats price with carter; gives birth to son Jozek Hollett, father Halan Hollett, family lives Dunholt; counts coins twice, comes up penny short); Aewyn, Seena Hollett, Rozek, Ridette, Jotho Corrett (sorts letters by candlelight), Halan/Halan Hollett, Ilrine Corrett, Wewyn Corrett (child born to Ridette Lindson and Jotho Corrett, lived Yarlton), Colan Lindson. Atmospheric details: threatening rain holding off, bees humming in lavender, light going early, dog barking then quiet, vespers bell, baker's boy late, line at oven grows long, cart with turnips, gulls over fish heads, river up in spring, salt price scandal.
